sections.paragraph: Itraconazole is an antifungal with several distinct cancer research programs. The clinical evidence includes small exploratory trials and uncontrolled chemotherapy series; other cancer findings remain preclinical. Itraconazole inhibits fungal ergosterol synthesis, impairing the fungal cell membrane. Its cancer-repurposing rationale involves several different actions: changing growth signals, restricting blood-vessel formation and disrupting mitochondrial energy metabolism. Hedgehog and WNT are signaling pathways involved in cell growth; angiogenesis is the formation of new blood vessels. The evidence ranges from experiments in cells and mice to pathway measurements in human tumors, so the biological explanation needs to be read alongside the model in which it was tested. Small studies found signals of activity in basal cell, prostate and lung cancers, but designs and endpoints differ.

sections.paragraph: Pramipexole is a dopamine agonist used for Parkinson’s disease and restless legs syndrome. PAX-D found improvement when it was added for treatment-resistant unipolar depression. Label context: Pramipexole stimulates the D2 family of dopamine receptors, with greater affinity for D3. The precise mechanisms of its Parkinson and restless-legs benefits remain incompletely understood; receptor binding alone does not establish an antidepressant effect. Clinical evidence: Low for the currently usable PAX-D result. The randomized trial reported greater improvement in depressive symptoms with pramipexole augmentation than placebo at twelve weeks. The existing assessment remains provisional because an indexed correction has not been reconciled. Adverse-event discontinuations were higher with pramipexole, and the trial does not establish superiority to another active augmentation treatment.

sections.paragraph: Mebendazole treats intestinal worm infections. Cancer research includes ovarian and oral-cell experiments plus glioma combination trials. Mebendazole interferes with parasite tubulin and microtubules, disrupting cellular transport and glucose uptake. In recurrent glioblastoma, neither mebendazole-containing regimen achieved its prespecified survival benchmark. Ovarian and oral-cancer findings cited here are experimental, without corresponding patient survival estimates. Mebendazole was tested in cell lines and patient-derived xenografts; these models assess antitumor activity without establishing a treatment effect in patients. Nine-month survival was 36.6% with temozolomide-mebendazole and 45% with lomustine-mebendazole, below the 55% benchmark; both arms included mebendazole. The oral-cancer cell study found changes in migration and cell-state markers, not clinical tumor response or survival. The glioblastoma trial compared two chemotherapy partners, so it cannot isolate the effect of adding mebendazole to either one.

sections.paragraph: Celecoxib treats pain and inflammatory conditions through COX-2 inhibition. Large breast and colon trials did not show overall disease-free survival benefit; smaller combination studies address different questions. Celecoxib selectively inhibits COX-2, reducing prostaglandin production involved in pain and inflammation. REACT did not improve breast-cancer disease-free survival, and CALGB/SWOG 80702 did not improve it overall in stage III colon cancer. A PIK3CA-defined colon subgroup and a small liver-cancer combination trial reported favorable findings; the latter cannot isolate celecoxib. Long COVID reports used multiple drugs without randomization. The 24 completers reported symptom improvements on valacyclovir-celecoxib with or without Paxlovid; convenience sampling and multiple drugs prevent attribution to celecoxib. DoCaCel found no significant progression-free or overall survival advantage, with interpretation limited by premature celecoxib discontinuation.

sections.paragraph: Glioblastoma is an aggressive glioma that infiltrates brain tissue. Treatment commonly combines surgery where feasible with radiation and chemotherapy, but infiltration makes complete removal difficult. Mebendazole, an antiparasitic medicine, has been investigated as an addition to temozolomide in newly diagnosed high-grade gliomas. A phase 1 study examined mebendazole with temozolomide, concentrating on dose, exposure and tolerability. The study did not randomize patients against temozolomide alone, so survival observations cannot establish an added survival benefit. This phase 1 study did not provide a controlled estimate of survival improvement. It also included high-grade gliomas beyond glioblastoma, making tumor classification important when reading individual outcomes. The phase 1 trial enrolled 24 people with high-grade gliomas, including 18 with glioblastoma.

This study does not compare itraconazole with curative local treatment or with approved Hedgehog-pathway drugs.

The congestive-heart-failure event occurred in a small exploratory treatment program. Only nineteen of twenty-nine enrolled participants received itraconazole, and the study was open-label. That limited treatment experience is the setting for the fatigue and cardiac observations, rather than a large controlled comparison designed to estimate the frequency of uncommon adverse events.

sections.paragraph: Acute myeloid leukemia is a fast-growing cancer of blood-forming cells in the bone marrow. Repurposing studies have explored medicines that alter the gene regulation of leukemia cells. In older adults unsuitable for intensive chemotherapy, a randomized trial did not find a survival advantage from adding valproate to decitabine. The factorial trial tested valproate and all-trans retinoic acid separately. Favorable remission and survival findings were associated with the retinoic-acid assignment, not valproate. The factorial design independently allocated the added medicines, allowing the valproate and retinoic-acid effects to be separated. A favorable result for one cannot be assigned to both. The factorial design separates the valproate question from the retinoic-acid question. It should not be summarized as though every drug in the combination produced the same result.

sections.paragraph: Schizophrenia can involve psychotic symptoms, reduced motivation and expression, and cognitive difficulties such as problems with attention or working memory. These symptom domains require different outcome measures. A small metformin add-on trial reported improved cognitive test performance. By contrast, the larger BeneMin trial found no benefit from minocycline for negative symptoms. At 24 weeks, the between-group difference in the MCCB composite score was 3.43 points (95% CI 1.83-5.02). The open-label trial randomized 72 people and lacked a placebo group. BeneMin randomized 207 people with recent-onset illness; the negative-symptom difference was −0.19 points (95% CI −1.23 to 0.85), showing no benefit over placebo. Metformin’s parent trial measured cognition; its companion report studied metabolites and imaging in smaller subsets.

sections.paragraph: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis damages the motor neurons that control voluntary muscles. Progressive weakness can affect movement, speech, swallowing and breathing. Clinical evidence: Moderate for harmful functional decline with the tested minocycline regimen. In the randomized 412-person ALS trial, function declined faster than with placebo during nine months. This primary outcome argues against the hoped-for neuroprotective benefit in that setting. ALSFRS-R scores fell by 1.30 points per month with minocycline versus 1.04 with placebo; the difference was statistically significant (P=0.005). The selected trial directly measured function, survival and safety. Its functional-harm assessment applies to the tested regimen; mortality and individual adverse-event risks retain separate uncertainty. Mortality evidence: Low for a difference. Mortality was numerically higher with minocycline, but the estimate was uncertain and not statistically significant.

sections.paragraph: Type 2 diabetes is a condition in which blood glucose remains too high because tissues do not respond adequately to insulin and the pancreas cannot supply enough insulin to compensate. Over time, diabetes can damage the eyes, kidneys, nerves and cardiovascular system. Management combines healthy daily habits, monitoring and medicines selected for the person’s glucose levels and other health conditions. Metformin is an established glucose-lowering treatment for type 2 diabetes, rather than an experimental repurposing use in this condition. Metformin is labeled as an addition to diet and exercise to improve blood glucose control in type 2 diabetes. Metformin reduces liver glucose output and intestinal glucose absorption while increasing glucose uptake and use in tissues. The renal restriction concerns the use of metformin, whereas glucose monitoring addresses the broader management of diabetes and its medicines.
